relations.subject: Shi Nenghai
relations.evidence: In 1917, Nenghai moved to Chengdu, capital of Sichuan province, founded the Shaocheng Society of Buddhist Studies (少城佛學社).

relations.subject: Shi Nenghai
relations.evidence: He became the main Chinese disciple of Khangsar Rinpoché (1890–1941) at Drepung monastery and was initiated into the tantric deities of Yellow Mañjuśrī and Yamāntaka-Vajrabhairava.

relations.subject: Shi Nenghai
relations.evidence: He was a member of the Permanent Committee and vice-president of the Chinese Buddhist Association from 1953 to 1966.
